answer: Co-staking resists sybils: to vouch for another identity you must co-bond your own collateral behind it, and if that identity is later slashed for fraud, your co-stake burns too. Endorsing a swarm is no longer free — a sparrow vouching for a plume of fakes puts its own capital at risk per endorsement. The oasis of cheap mutual-vouching dries up: an attacker's accounts can still vouch for each other, but doing so chains all their bonds together, so one caught fake can cascade-slash the whole cluster's stake.
